# Working with the File System

Command-line utilities spend a significant percentage of their runtime interacting with the filesystem: locating paths, inspecting metadata, streaming large files, and walking directory trees.

## Path Manipulations with `Path` and `PathBuf`

Rust separates borrowed paths (`&Path`) from owned, heap-allocated paths (`PathBuf`), mirroring `&str` and `String`:

```rust
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

fn inspect_path(p: &Path) {
    println!("File name: {:?}", p.file_name());
    println!("Extension: {:?}", p.extension());
    println!("Parent dir: {:?}", p.parent());
    println!("Is absolute: {}", p.is_absolute());
}

fn build_target_path(base: &Path, filename: &str) -> PathBuf {
    base.join("logs").join(filename)
}
```

## Efficient File Reading and Writing

For small files, `std::fs::read_to_string` and `std::fs::write` are convenient:

```rust
use std::fs;
use std::io;

fn quick_read(path: &str) -> io::Result<String> {
    fs::read_to_string(path)
}
```

For large files, avoid reading the entire payload into RAM at once. Use `BufReader` and stream line by line:

```rust
use std::fs::File;
use std::io::{self, BufRead, BufReader};
use std::path::Path;

fn count_non_empty_lines(path: &Path) -> io::Result<usize> {
    let file = File::open(path)?;
    let reader = BufReader::new(file);
    let mut count = 0;

    for line in reader.lines() {
        let line = line?;
        if !line.trim().is_empty() {
            count += 1;
        }
    }
    Ok(count)
}
```

## Fast Directory Traversal with `walkdir`

When building search or indexing tools like `find` or `fd`, recursive directory traversal using `std::fs::read_dir` requires complex recursion and symlink handling. The `walkdir` crate provides an optimized, configurable iterator:

```toml
[dependencies]
walkdir = "2.5"
```

```rust
use walkdir::WalkDir;
use std::path::Path;

fn find_rs_files(dir: &Path) {
    for entry in WalkDir::new(dir)
        .follow_links(false)
        .max_depth(5)
        .into_iter()
        .filter_map(Result::ok)
    {
        if entry.file_type().is_file() {
            if let Some(ext) = entry.path().extension() {
                if ext == "rs" {
                    println!("Found Rust file: {}", entry.path().display());
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```
